artifact_revision: agentmux 121d29ac + session-10 working tree; installed asl 0.2.0 (/Users/sglavoie/.local/bin/asl) serving contract set asl-amx-1.85ec3041b9f03f47, bridge protocol 2; tmux 3.7c on a private server; macOS 27.0.1
method: `just asl-integration` equivalent run verbosely: AMX_ASL_INTEGRATION=1 go test -count=1 -v -run TestInstalledBridge ./internal/aslbridge ./internal/daemon. TestInstalledBridgeRoutesRunsByRuntimeSession builds this checkout's amx into a throwaway HOME, serves that HOME's daemon socket from an in-process daemon Handler over the real IPC server, and runs two real `asl run`s (throwaway plans, throwaway Git repositories, isolated state root) whose lifecycle and mailbox hooks arrive through the real `amx hook-indicator` client. Real: asl and its mailbox/hooks/projection/bridge, the amx hook client and IPC dedupe, the daemon handler/reducer/notifier decision path, the private tmux server and pane, the runtime-session registry and checkpoint. Stand-ins: the harness is a script that asks one mailbox question with `asl ask --wait` and then completes its session; the notification backend is a recorder (no macOS alert is shown); the Kitty instance is a fixed window listing, because Kitty launches do not register runtime sessions yet and an isolated test must not drive the operator's Kitty. No desktop viewer exists yet, so viewer absence is a daemon with no Kitty client, no companion subscriber, and no client attached to the tmux server.

tmux-asl.evidence: A real `asl run` executing as the pane process of a tmux runtime session (launched with session.LaunchOn on a private tmux 3.7c server, registered in a real runtime-session registry) delivered its lifecycle hooks as runtime session rs-09001ad17cb8b1b1d0a610e6b6c97506: run 20261010T000249795444Z-67009's lease went live on that session's non-Kitty slot while the daemon had no Kitty client at all. Its worker's mailbox question, surfaced by `asl outbox wait` from the same session, raised the question icon on that slot; `asl inbox reply` cleared it; the run's end released the lease. Hermetic counterpart TestASLRunInTmuxSessionRoutesToItsRuntimeSlot additionally shows a managed Kitty tab in the same directory and harness, and an inherited kitty_window_id naming it, receive no state. Logs: session-10/asl-integration-v.log (OBSERVED tmux-asl, misrouting check), session-10/daemon-runtime-asl-v.log.

daemon-restart.evidence: While the tmux run was still blocked on its question, the first daemon flushed its runtime checkpoint and stopped serving; a new Handler restored the checkpoint and served the same socket. Observed after restart: runtime session rs-09001ad17cb8b1b1d0a610e6b6c97506 bound to a non-Kitty slot again, run 20261010T000249795444Z-67009's lease live, icon after restore "question". The still-open question, resurfaced to the new daemon by `asl outbox wait` and followed by a reconcile sweep, showed the question icon with 0 new notifications; the later reply and the run's end were both applied by the restarted daemon. Log: session-10/asl-integration-v.log (OBSERVED daemon-restart, misrouting check).
